title: Volume Analysis: The Correct Way to Read & Understand the Market

events.ocr:
What Do You Actually See?
When you look at a price chart...
events.description: A hand-drawn illustration shows a stick figure looking thoughtfully at a candlestick price chart. A large, orange question mark is superimposed over the center of the chart, representing confusion or the challenge of interpretation. The style is simple and sketch-like on a textured white background.

events.text: Hello everyone! Let me ask you a question.
When you look at a price chart,  what do you actually see?
Most traders see candles going up and down.
They see patterns. They see lines.
But they're missing the most important  piece of information on the entire chart.
Volume. Price is just the advertisement.
Volume is the actual transaction. It's like judging a restaurant
only by its sign outside, without ever  checking if there are any customers inside.
In this video, I'm going to show  you how to read volume correctly.
Not just what volume is. But what it MEANS.
Why it matters. And how to use it to see
what's really happening behind every move. After this video, every candle on your
chart will tell you a story. And volume will be the proof.
Not financial advice. Just education.
Let's get into it. Let's start with the basics.
Every chart speaks two languages at the same time. Language number one: Price.

events.ocr:
1
PRICE
Language #1: PRICE
The WHAT
WHAT Happened?
Up? Down? Sideways?
NEWS
events.description: A hand-drawn illustration features a stick figure on the left pointing upward. To its right, a candlestick chart shows a distinct upward trend, overlaid with a large green arrow pointing up and to the right. In the bottom right corner is a small icon of a newspaper, and the top left corner features the number 1 inside a circle.

events.text: Price tells you WHAT happened. Did the market go up?
Down? Sideways?
That's the headline. The news title.
Language number two: Volume. Volume tells you HOW MUCH
conviction was behind that move. How many traders participated?
How much money actually moved there? That's the evidence.
The proof. Think of it like an election.
Price is the result — who won. But volume is the number of voters who showed up.
If only 10 people voted, does  the result really mean anything?
But if 10 million people  voted — that's a declaration.
Same with the market. A big green candle on low volume?
Suspicious. A big green candle on high volume?
That's conviction. That's real.
From now on, every time you look at a  chart, don't just ask: "Where did price go?"
Also ask: "How much money stood behind that move?" Now here's the single most important idea
in this entire video. To read volume correctly,

events.ocr:
ONE Mental Model
1
EFFORT vs RESULT
events.description: A whiteboard-style illustration introduces a concept. The title "ONE Mental Model" is above a large blue number "1" inside a circle. Below this, the phrase "EFFORT vs RESULT" is enclosed in a box, with radiating lines emphasizing both the number and the phrase. A simple stick figure in the bottom-left corner points up enthusiastically towards the main concept.

events.text: you only need ONE mental model. Just one.
Effort versus Result. In the market:
Effort is volume — how much energy,  how much money is being used.
Result is the candle — how  far price actually moved.
Think of it like pushing a car up a hill. Your foot on the gas pedal is the effort.
How far the car moves is the result. Case number one: You press the gas.
The car moves easily. Big effort.
Big result. Everything matches.
On the chart, that's a big candle  with high volume underneath.
Lots of buyers. Lots of conviction.
The move is real. Like a whole stadium standing up to cheer.
That's genuine excitement. Case number two: You slam the gas pedal.
The engine roars. Fuel is burning.
But the car barely moves. There's something blocking the road.
On the chart, that's a tiny candle  with MASSIVE volume underneath.
This is called Absorption. What's happening?
Buyers are pushing hard, but  there's an invisible wall.

events.ocr:
ABSORPTION
Big Effort • Small Result
Warning Sign
The Invisible Wall
Warning Sign
events.description: The image presents a concept called "Absorption" using two diagrams. The left diagram shows a financial candlestick chart where high volume leads to small price increases, which is labeled a "Warning Sign." The right diagram provides an analogy, depicting a large wave crashing against a dam labeled "The Invisible Wall," also identified as a "Warning Sign," to illustrate market resistance absorbing buying pressure.

events.text: A large seller — smart money — is sitting  there, quietly absorbing every single buy order.
Think of a dam. The water keeps
pouring in, but the dam holds everything back. When the water runs out — when buyers exhaust
themselves — there's nobody left to push price up. And very often, price drops sharply.
Case number three: You barely touch the gas. But the car keeps rolling uphill by itself.
There's no resistance. The road is empty.
On the chart, that's price  moving up on LOW volume.
This is called No Supply. It doesn't mean buyers are super strong.
It means sellers are ABSENT. Nobody is selling.
So the market doesn't need much effort to move. Like walking on an empty road.
No one is blocking your path. Now here's your cheat sheet.
The Volume Matrix. High volume plus big candle — healthy move.

events.ocr:
VOLUME MATRIX
Your Cheat Sheet
HEALTHY
Big + Big = Real
ABSORPTION
Big + Small = Warning
NO SUPPLY
Move + Low = Absent
events.description: A diagram titled "Volume Matrix" presents a cheat sheet with three illustrated panels. The "Healthy" panel shows large green price and volume candlesticks with a checkmark. The "Absorption" panel displays a small red price candle over a large orange volume bar with a warning icon. The "No Supply" panel features an upward-trending blue line graph over a small blue volume bar, accompanied by an information icon and a pointing stick figure.

events.text: High volume plus small candle — absorption. Warning sign.
Low volume plus price still  moving — no supply or no demand.
The other side is absent. Memorize these three combinations.
They're the foundation of  everything that comes next.
Now let's apply Effort vs Result  to specific candle patterns.
This is Volume Spread Analysis — VSA. Three patterns every trader should recognize.
Pattern one: Stopping Volume. Imagine price is crashing.
Red candle after red candle. Everyone is panicking and selling.
Then you see this: a tall red candle,  the volume bar underneath is HUGE — the
biggest in weeks. But here's the thing.
The candle doesn't close at the very bottom. It has a long wick below, and the close is
near the middle. What happened?
Someone with deep pockets bought EVERYTHING  the panicking sellers were throwing away.
They didn't stop the crash with words. They stopped it with money.

events.ocr:
PANIC SELLERS
STOPPED
POTENTIAL REVERSAL
Smart Money Absorbing
High Effort • Small Result
= Reversal Zone
$
events.description: A cartoon diagram illustrates a financial market concept. A large red downward arrow, representing a price drop, is halted by a large blue money bag, symbolizing 'smart money' absorbing the selling pressure from 'panic sellers'. Panicked stick figures are shown running away from the downward arrow. Text labels indicate this is a 'Reversal Zone' and points to a 'POTENTIAL REVERSAL'.

events.text: High effort. Small result.
The price didn't go lower despite massive volume. That's absorption at the bottom.
A potential reversal zone. Pattern two: Buying Climax.
Now imagine the opposite. Price has been going up for weeks.
News is great. Everyone is bullish.
Retail traders are jumping in  because they don't want to miss out.
Then you see: a huge green candle. Volume is EXTREME — the
highest on the entire chart. To most traders, this looks like massive strength.
But here's the plot twist. This is NOT strong buying.
This is strong selling DISGUISED as buying. Smart money uses that wall of buy orders from
retail traders to unload their massive positions. They're selling INTO the demand, quietly,
without crashing the price. Like a vendor at a night market.
The busiest moment? That's when they're
clearing out the last of their stock. The moment you FOMO in at the top?

events.ocr:
PLOT TWIST
NOT Buying - It's Selling DISGUISED
Smart Money Exit
events.description: A cartoon depicts a market stall where a vendor with a cunning expression hands out boxes to an eager crowd. To the right, a character labeled "Smart Money Exit" walks away with a briefcase and cash. The scene illustrates a concept where a buying frenzy among the general public is actually an opportunity for insiders to sell their holdings and take profits.

events.text: That might be exactly when smart  money is walking out the door.
Pattern three: No Supply Test. After an uptrend, price pulls back a little.
You're worried. "Is this a correction?"
Then you look at volume: a small  red candle, and volume is VERY low.
The market is asking a question:  "Does anyone want to sell here?"
And low volume answers: "No. Not really." That's a No Supply test.
Sellers are absent. The uptrend is likely to continue.
Like testing if the fire is hot. You put your hand near it — it's cool.
Safe to move forward. Three patterns.
One mental model. Effort versus Result.
That's enough to read eighty percent of  what volume is telling you on any chart.
Now, before we go further, let me clear up  the most common mistake in volume reading.
And if you've been making  this mistake, don't worry.
Almost everyone does. The myth: "Green volume bar means

events.ocr:
THE MYTH
Green = Buying?
WRONG
Red = Selling?
events.description: A hand-drawn style illustration debunks a common belief about market indicators. On the left, a green bar is labeled "Green = Buying?", and on the right, a red bar is labeled "Red = Selling?". A large red 'X' is drawn over both bars with the word "WRONG" in the center, indicating this belief is false. A confused stick figure with a question mark over its head stands below, reinforcing the theme of questioning this myth.

events.text: buying. Red volume bar means selling." That is NOT how it works.
Here's the truth. Every single trade requires a buyer AND a seller.
Always. Without exception.
If you bought 100 shares, someone  else SOLD you those 100 shares.
Volume counts the NUMBER of transactions. Not which "side" is winning.
The color of the volume bar? It simply follows the color of the candle.
If the candle closed higher  than it opened — green bar.
If it closed lower — red bar. That's it.
It has nothing to do with who  is buying or who is selling.
Think of a busy fish market  at five in the morning.
The market is packed — high volume. But there are buyers AND sellers everywhere.
You can't say "today is all buying"  just because the market is busy.
Busy means activity. To know who is WINNING,
you look at where the candle closes. So here's the rule:
Don't look at the COLOR of the volume bar. Look at the SIZE of the volume bar, combined
with where the candle closes. Size plus close position.

events.ocr:
THE RULE
Don't → Color X
DO → Size + Close ✓
Size
← Close
SIZE + CLOSE = The Real Story
events.description: A hand-drawn diagram contrasts two approaches to financial chart analysis. On the left, under the heading "Don't → Color", two colored volume bars are crossed out with a large red X. On the right, under "DO → Size + Close", a large volume bar is labeled "Size" next to two candlestick charts, with an arrow pointing to the closing price labeled "Close". A stick figure gives a thumbs-up next to a box at the bottom summarizing the main point: "SIZE + CLOSE = The Real Story".

events.text: That's where the real story is. Now let's talk about one of the most powerful
warning signals in volume analysis. Volume Divergence.
When price and volume agree with  each other, the trend is healthy.
Price going up? Volume going up?
Strong. Price going down?
Volume going down? The selling is weakening.
But when price and volume DISAGREE  — that's your early warning system.
Here's the most important one. Imagine price is making new highs.
The chart looks great. Everyone is celebrating.
But if you look at the volume  bars, they're getting SMALLER.
Each new high has LESS  volume than the previous one.
Think of a rocket. At launch, the fuel is full.
The rocket blasts off with enormous power. But as the fuel burns, the thrust weakens.
The rocket slows down. And eventually... it falls.
That's what declining volume  during an uptrend looks like.

events.ocr:
DIVERGENCE = WARNING
Price ↑
Volume ↓
Higher Highs • Lower Volume
FULL
LOW
EMPTY
Fuel Depleting = Crash Coming
Move Running Out of Fuel
events.description: A hand-drawn infographic explains bearish divergence in trading. The left side displays a candlestick price chart making higher highs, while the corresponding volume chart below shows declining volume, indicating a warning. The right side uses a metaphor of a rocket running out of fuel to represent this weakening trend, showing three stages: a rocket ascending with a full tank, a sputtering rocket with a low tank, and a crashing rocket with an empty tank.

events.text: The move is running out of fuel. Fewer and fewer traders believe in the move.
The same works in reverse. If price is falling but volume keeps
dropping too — sellers are getting exhausted. Each drop has less and less participation.
The selling is drying up. That often signals a bottom is forming.
Volume divergence is your  free early warning system.
The market hasn't crashed yet. But it's getting tired.
It's like the applause getting  quieter after each speech.
The audience is losing interest. The show is almost over.
When you see price making new highs but  volume making lower highs — pay attention.
Something is about to change. Now let's turn everything into
a simple process you can use on any  chart, any market, starting today.
I call it the 3-Step Volume Check. Step one: Zoom Out.
Before you look at individual candles,  zoom out to the daily or weekly chart.

events.ocr:
1 STEP 1: Zoom Out
Volume Trend?
Overall Trend?
Check Weather = Check Climate
Know the Big Picture First
events.description: The slide is titled "STEP 1: Zoom Out." It displays a candlestick chart with a corresponding volume chart below, both indicating an overall upward trend. A magnifying glass with a minus sign is positioned over the chart, and to the right, a stick figure points to an analogy comparing checking the weather to checking the climate, represented by a sun and a cloud.

events.text: Ask yourself: Is volume overall  increasing or decreasing?
Are there any unusual volume spikes recently?
Think of it like checking the  weather before going outside.
You want to know the climate  before you worry about the rain.
Step two: Zoom In to Key Levels. Find the important support and
resistance levels on your chart. Now watch what happens when price
approaches those levels. Apply Effort vs Result.
If price touches resistance and volume SPIKES  but the candle stays small — that's absorption.
The wall is holding. Be careful.
If price breaks through resistance with a big  candle AND high volume — that's a real breakout.
Effort matches result. But if price breaks
resistance on LOW volume — be suspicious. A breakout without conviction is often a trap.
Step three: Wait for Confirmation. This is where most traders go wrong.
They see one signal and immediately jump in. Don't do that.

events.ocr:
3 STEP 3: Wait for Confirmation
Resistance (becomes Support)
Breakout
Wait... Pullback?
Confirmed ✓
Low Volume = No Supply
Breakout → Wait → Test → Confirmed
1 Candle Patience = 10 Trades Saved
PATIENCE
events.description: A hand-drawn infographic explains a stock trading concept using a candlestick chart. The chart shows a price breaking above a resistance line, followed by a small pullback which tests the old resistance line as new support. A meditating stick figure labeled "PATIENCE" sits next to the chart, emphasizing the importance of waiting for this confirmation before trading.

events.text: After a breakout, wait for the next candle. Does price pull back to the broken level?
If it does, and that pullback happens  on LOW volume — that's a No Supply test.
The market tested the level and found no sellers. That's your confirmation.
Patience for one extra candle can  save you from ten losing trades.
Let me show you how this looks in practice. Price is approaching resistance.
You zoom out — volume has been steady. Price touches resistance.
Volume spikes. But the candle is small with a long upper wick.
High effort, small result. Absorption.
The wall is strong. You don't buy.
You wait. Price drops.
You avoided a trap. Three steps.
Zoom out. Zoom in to key levels.
Wait for confirmation. That's your volume playbook.
Before your next trade, run  through this quick checklist.
One: Is volume increasing or  decreasing compared to recent bars?

events.ocr:
5 Questions to Ask
1. Volume trend? (↑ or ↓ vs recent)
2. Effort = Result? (Absorption?)
Absorption if mismatch
3. Spikes at key levels?
4. Divergence? (New highs + lower vol)
Lower highs = warning
5. Next candle confirms?
Never act on 1 candle
events.description: A hand-drawn illustration on a white background presents a checklist titled "5 Questions to Ask". The five questions are listed with numbered bullet points and checkboxes. To the right of the list stands a simple stick figure. Key terms within the list are visually emphasized with an orange circle, a yellow underline, and a blue box.

events.text: Two: Does the effort match the result? Big volume should mean big candles — if not,
someone is absorbing. Three: Are there any
unusual volume spikes near key levels? Four: Is volume diverging from price?
New highs on lower volume is a warning. Five: What does the next candle confirm?
Never act on one candle alone. When you ask these five questions,
you're no longer guessing. You're reading the market.
You're seeing the proof behind every move. Because volume is not just
another indicator on your chart. Volume is the truth serum of the market.
Price can be pushed around. Price can be manipulated.
But volume shows you where real money  — real commitment — is stepping in.
If this video helped you finally see what's  behind the candles, let me know in the comments.
Which pattern are you going to look for first? Stopping Volume?
Buying Climax? Or Volume Divergence?
Drop a comment. I read every single one.
I'll see you in the next video. Stay disciplined.
